name: Auvrenth Text-to-Speech Reader
author: Auvrenth Studio

sections.description:
Auvrenth Text-to-Speech Reader adds a listen button to your posts and pages. Visitors press play and the article is read aloud by the voices already built into their browser.

It needs no account, no API key and no monthly cost, and it stores no audio files on your server. The speech is made on the visitor’s own device, so nothing is sent to an outside service.

Want a natural voice that sounds the same for everyone? Activate an AI voice add-on (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google Cloud or Azure) under Auvrenth Reader → Add-ons and use its voices with your own API key.

For visitors

  • Play, pause and stop. Stopping keeps the visitor’s place: the button turns into Resume and carries on from the word where reading stopped, where the voice reports its position.
  • Skip to the previous or next sentence, or click the progress bar to jump ahead.
  • Reading speed control, and a language and voice switcher whose choice is remembered.
  • The sentence being read is highlighted in the article, and the page scrolls along with it. Scrolling by hand pauses the following for a few seconds.
  • A mini player stays at the bottom of the screen when the player scrolls out of view while listening.
  • Keyboard friendly: the left and right arrow keys skip sentences while the player has focus, and every button has a tooltip and a screen reader label.
  • Remembers where a visitor stopped and offers “Continue where you stopped” on their next visit.
  • Sleep timer (5 to 60 minutes, or end of article), a “Jump to section” list of the article’s headings, and volume and pitch sliders.
  • Select any passage in the article and press the small “Listen” button to hear just that part.

For site owners

  • Choose the post types, and show the player before or after the content.
  • Set a default language, voice, speed and pitch, and test them right from the settings screen.
  • Uses a voice that matches your site language when the browser has one.
  • Turn sentence highlighting, page scrolling, the mini player and the language switcher on or off.
  • Match your site with the play button color, the play icon color and the title and control color.
  • Hide the player on single posts, or place it anywhere with the Auvrenth Player block or the [auvrenth_tts] shortcode.
  • Change what is read aloud with the auvrenth_tts_text filter.
  • Product short descriptions are read before the long description.

AI voice add-ons (built in, each off until you activate it)

  • Hosted MP3 audio from ElevenLabs, from OpenAI, or from any OpenAI-compatible speech service, with your own API key.
  • Pick an ElevenLabs voice and model from your account, tune stability, similarity, style and speaker boost, and see how many characters you have used this billing period.
  • The audio is made in the background when a post is published or its text changes, or only when you tick “Make audio” in the editor box.
  • Long posts are sent in pieces, and after an edit only the pieces whose text changed are sent again, so you only pay for what changed.
  • Visitors get a “Download MP3” link in the player.

The player only appears in browsers that support speech synthesis, which covers all current versions of Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox. Sentence highlighting needs a browser with the CSS Custom Highlight API: current Chrome, Edge and Safari, and Firefox 140 or later. Everything else works without it.

Auvrenth Player block and shortcode

Add the Auvrenth Player block (in the block inserter under Media, or search for “Auvrenth”), or [auvrenth_tts] in a post, page or Shortcode block, to show the player exactly where you want it. It reads the post it is placed in.

  • The editor shows the player as visitors will see it, and the block sidebar changes that one player only: the button label, default speed, sentence highlighting, page scrolling, the mini player, and the play button, play icon and text colors. Anything left on “site setting” follows the settings screen.
  • The block also has the usual margin and HTML anchor settings.
  • Works on any post type, even ones not ticked under “Show on” in the settings.
  • When a post contains the block or the shortcode, the automatic player is skipped there, so the player never shows twice.
  • Set “Player position” to “Only where I add the [auvrenth_tts] shortcode” to turn off automatic placement everywhere and use the block or shortcode only.
  • The block and shortcode show nothing when the player is hidden for that post in the editor, or when the post is password protected.

External services

This plugin connects to an outside speech service only when you activate one of the AI voice add-ons and choose it as the audio source under Auvrenth Reader → AI voices. Until then, nothing is sent anywhere.

ElevenLabs

Used when the audio source is ElevenLabs, to turn post text into speech.

  • When a post is published or updated (or when you tick “Make audio”), the post’s title and text are sent with your API key to api.elevenlabs.io to make the MP3.
  • When you open the AI voices screen, your API key is sent to list your voices and models and show the characters used this billing period.

ElevenLabs Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible service

Used when the audio source is an OpenAI-compatible speech service. When a post is published or updated (or when you tick “Make audio”), the post’s title and text are sent with your API key to the service address you enter (by default api.openai.com) to make the MP3.

OpenAI Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. If you enter another service’s address, that service’s own terms apply.

Google Cloud Text-to-Speech

Used when the audio source is Google. When a post is published or updated (or when you tick “Make audio”), the post’s title and text are sent with your API key to texttospeech.googleapis.com to make the MP3.

Google Cloud Terms of Service and Privacy Notice.

Microsoft Azure Speech

Used when the audio source is Azure. When a post is published or updated (or when you tick “Make audio”), the post’s title and text are sent with your subscription key to {region}.tts.speech.microsoft.com to make the MP3.

Microsoft Terms of Use and Privacy Statement.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the auvrenth-text-to-speech-reader folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Auvrenth Reader in the admin menu. Its screens are Player, Voice, Listener tools and Add-ons.
sections.faq:
Does it need an API key?

No. Speech is generated by the visitor’s browser, so nothing is sent to an outside service. An API key is only needed if you activate the AI Voices add-on.

Can I use AI voices such as ElevenLabs or OpenAI?

Yes. Go to Auvrenth Reader → Add-ons and activate the service you want: ElevenLabs Voices, OpenAI Voices, Google Cloud Voices or Azure Voices. Then open Auvrenth Reader → AI voices, choose it as the audio source, add your own API key and pick a voice. Each post gets a natural-sounding MP3 that visitors can play and download. The add-on is free; the speech service bills you directly for what you use. While AI Voices is off, this plugin never contacts an outside service.

Why does the voice sound different on another device?

Each browser and operating system ships its own voices, so the voice depends on the visitor’s device.

How do visitors change the volume?

The player has a volume slider in its settings panel. Some online or “natural” browser voices ignore it, so the device’s own volume controls always work too. You can turn the slider off under Listener tools.

Why does the pitch setting not change some voices?

The default pitch is passed to the browser, but some voices, such as many online or “natural” voices, ignore it and always use their own pitch. The speed setting works with all voices.

How do I place the player in a different spot?

Add the Auvrenth Player block, or the [auvrenth_tts] shortcode, where the player should appear. To use it in a theme template, call <?php echo do_shortcode( '[auvrenth_tts]' ); ?> inside the loop and set “Player position” to the shortcode-only option, so the automatic player does not show as well.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. Auvrenth Text-to-Speech Reader Pro adds a pronunciation dictionary (used by browser voices and AI voices), skip rules for code, tables and CSS classes, anonymous play counts, and an “Up next” link. It needs this plugin to be active.

Can I change what is read aloud?

Yes. Use the auvrenth_tts_text filter to change the text for any post. Line breaks in the text separate blocks such as headings and list items.

Why is a sentence not highlighted?

The player highlights a sentence when it finds the same words on the page. Text that is not shown on the page, such as a title the theme displays elsewhere or text changed with the auvrenth_tts_text filter, is still read but not highlighted.

Can I turn off the highlighting or the page scrolling?

Yes. Under “While listening” in the settings you can turn off sentence highlighting, page scrolling and the mini player separately.

Can I change the colors?

Yes. The settings screen has color pickers for the play button, the icon inside it, and the title and control icons. The Auvrenth Player block can set its own colors for one player. Themes can also restyle the player with the CSS custom properties --auvrenth-tts-accent, --auvrenth-tts-accent-text and --auvrenth-tts-highlight.

Can one post look or behave differently from the rest?

Yes. Add the Auvrenth Player block to that post and change its settings in the block sidebar. Anything left on “site setting” keeps following the settings screen. To remove the player from a post altogether, tick “Hide the listen button on this page” in the “Auvrenth Text-to-Speech Reader” box in the editor.

What does it store about visitors?

In the visitor’s own browser’s local storage: the language, voice, volume and pitch they pick and where they stopped in each post. No cookies are set and nothing is sent to your server or to any outside service. The AI Voices add-on never sends anything from visitors’ browsers either: the post text is sent from your server when you save a post. (The separate Pro add-on can count plays; see its own notes.)

What happens to my settings if I delete the plugin?

Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen removes its settings, the per-post “hide the player” switches, and the AI Voices settings and MP3 files in uploads/auvrenth-tts. Deactivating the plugin, or deactivating the AI Voices add-on, keeps them.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: every AI service is now its own add-on with its own switch: ElevenLabs Voices, OpenAI Voices, Google Cloud Voices and Azure Voices. The AI voices screen shows only the services you turned on, and a service that is off keeps its saved settings. Sites that had the old AI Voices add-on on get the services they were using switched on automatically.
  • New: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech and Microsoft Azure Speech as hosted MP3 sources (Bangla supported).
  • New: Podcast RSS feed at /feed/auvrenth-podcast/ of posts that have hosted MP3 audio.
  • New: Content & podcast screen: read title and content, content only, or title only; skip code, tables, menus and chosen CSS classes (or any element with the class auvrenth-tts-skip).
  • New: Anonymous play counts per post, shown in a Listens column on the posts list.
  • New: Voice type (female or male) in the player and as a site preference.
  • New: Play button shape and size settings.
  • New: The Space bar plays and pauses while the visitor is listening.
  • New: Translation template in languages/.
  • New: Auvrenth Reader → Add-ons screen. Each add-on has a card with an on/off switch and a status line that says what it still needs or that it is ready. An add-on that is off loads none of its code and sends nothing anywhere.
  • New: AI Voices add-on, free and built in, off until you switch it on. It makes a hosted MP3 of each post from ElevenLabs, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible speech service, with your own API key.
  • AI Voices: choose an ElevenLabs voice and model from your account, tune stability, similarity, style and speaker boost, and see the characters used this billing period. Settings are under Auvrenth Reader → AI voices.
  • AI Voices: audio is made in the background when a post is published or its text changes, or only when you tick “Make audio” in the editor box. Long posts are sent in pieces, and after an edit only the changed pieces are sent again.
  • AI Voices: the editor box shows the audio status and has a “Regenerate audio” switch, and visitors get a Download MP3 link in the player.
  • Hosted audio moved here from Pro 1.0. Sites that used it in Pro get AI Voices switched on automatically and keep their API keys, voice, model, tuning and existing MP3 files. While Pro 1.0 is still active, AI Voices waits so audio is never made twice.
  • New auvrenth_tts_spoken_text filter for the text sent to the speech service.
  • Deleting the plugin now also removes the AI Voices settings, the audio information on posts and the MP3 files in uploads/auvrenth-tts.
  • New: continue where you stopped, sleep timer, jump to section, volume and pitch sliders, listen to selected text, WooCommerce short descriptions, separate settings screens, and hooks (auvrenth_tts_content, auvrenth_tts_player_data, auvrenth_tts_audio_url, auvrenth_tts_l10n, auvrenth_tts_panel_end, auvrenth_tts_player_end, auvrenth_tts_metabox) for the Pro add-on.

1.0.0

  • First release.
  • Listen button for posts and pages that reads the article aloud with the browser’s own voices. No API key and no audio files.
  • Player controls: play, pause, stop (keeps the visitor’s place and turns into Resume, which carries on from the word where reading stopped), previous and next sentence, click the progress bar to jump, and reading speed.
  • Sentence highlighting, with page scrolling that follows the reading and steps aside when the visitor scrolls by hand.
  • Mini player pinned to the bottom of the screen when the player scrolls out of view while listening.
  • Language and voice switcher in the player, remembered for the visitor’s next visit.
  • Left and right arrow keys skip sentences, and every button has a tooltip and a screen reader label.
  • Settings screen: post types, player position, button label, default speed, pitch, language and voice with a test button, highlighting, page scrolling, mini player, language switcher, and a volume note.
  • Color settings for the play button, the play icon, and the title and control icons.
  • Auvrenth Player block with a live preview in the editor and its own settings for the label, speed, highlighting, scrolling, mini player and colors, plus the [auvrenth_tts] shortcode to place the player anywhere, and a per-post switch to hide it.
  • auvrenth_tts_text filter to change what is read aloud.
